extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure only.
- **Deployment path:** GitHub Actions workflow named **“Deploy to Azure”**.
- **Triggers:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch`, which means deployments can be initiated automatically on code changes and manually.
- **Runners:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted runner.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** No region, zone, or multi-region configuration is shown. `availability_zones` is empty, and no redundancy or failover controls are visible in the provided data.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- The Azure credential principal is represented as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`, which indicates GitHub Actions secret storage rather than plaintext in the workflow.
- **Risk:** The deployment relies on a long-lived secret-backed credential instead of federated identity. This increases exposure if repository secrets are accessed or exfiltrated.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false`.
- No key management details, CMK/KMS integration, or storage encryption configuration are provided.
- **Assessment:** At-rest encryption cannot be confirmed from the supplied configuration, and no customer-managed key posture is visible.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity` is declared, but the principal is still sourced from `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`, so the configuration does not show a native Azure workload identity / OIDC federation flow.
- **Trust principal:** `github-actions`.
- **Scope:** `subscription`, which is broad and may exceed least-privilege requirements for a CI/CD deployment pipeline.
- **Assessment:** The visible IAM scope is high-risk due to subscription-wide access and the lack of OIDC-based short-lived credentials.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted GitHub Actions runner.
- **OIDC:** `uses_oidc: false`.
- **Trigger surface:** `push` plus `workflow_dispatch` increases the attack surface for deployment execution, especially if branch protection and environment approvals are not enforced elsewhere.
- **Assessment:** The workflow depends on GitHub Actions secrets and does not use OIDC, so credential lifetime and secret handling are weaker than a federated setup.

### 6) Container security
- No container/runtime nodes, container image settings, health checks, resource limits, or privilege settings are present in the provided data.
- **Therefore:** root user, missing health checks, and resource-limit status cannot be determined from this configuration snapshot.

### 7) Key risks and recommendations
1. **Replace secret-based Azure auth with OIDC federation**
   - Move from `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` to GitHub Actions OIDC / Azure workload identity federation.
   - This removes long-lived cloud credentials from repository secrets.

2. **Reduce IAM scope from subscription-wide access**
   - Re-scope permissions to the minimum Azure resource group / resource-level permissions required for deployment.
   - Validate the deployment principal cannot modify unrelated subscription assets.

3. **Harden GitHub Actions deployment controls**
   - Restrict `workflow_dispatch` to trusted operators and protect deployment branches.
   - Add environment protection, approval gates, and ensure secrets are not exposed to untrusted workflow contexts.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points:** `FastAPI` exposes `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, and `Chat Endpoint`. `Bearer Auth` protects all of these endpoints, plus `Generic`.

- **Orchestration flow:** `OpenAI Agents` invokes the agents `Triage`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Cancellation`. `Triage` further delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`.

- **Model usage:** `gpt-4.1-mini` is used by `Relevance Guardrail`, `Jailbreak Guardrail`, and all four task agents plus `Triage Agent`.

- **Tool access:** Multiple agents can call the same tools. `Triage`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, and `Cancellation` each call `Baggage Tool`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup Tool`, and `Flight Status Tool`. `OpenAI Agents` can also call `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat`.

- **Guardrails:** Only `Relevance Guardrail` and `Jailbreak Guardrail` are shown, and both use the model directly. The graph does not show explicit guardrail enforcement on agents or tools.

- **Data stores:** `Sqlite` appears in the graph but has **no connections**, so no datastore access path is shown.

- **Security observations:** Several tools are reachable from multiple agents and from the framework itself, which broadens the attack surface. No datastore or tool-level authorization is shown beyond endpoint bearer auth.
